topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final session of the course and sets out the learning objectives for cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the mechanisms, clinical utility, and resistance pathways associated with conventional cancer treatments such as surgery, radiation, and cytotoxic chemotherapy.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities and defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies designed to exploit inherent cancer cell vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and synthetic lethality.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of targeted drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the targeting of hyperactive oncogenic kinases with small-molecule inhibitors and the molecular bypass mechanisms that drive drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugate strategies used to target surface antigens on tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-directed therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how endogenous and engineered immune mechanisms are harnessed to detect and eliminate tumor cells.

topics.label: Clinical challenges, historical progress, and future paradigms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on historical mortality trends, current translational dilemmas, and future strategies in oncology management.
